summary: ⚠️ This snapshot is PRE-RESULTS — Firefly reports Q2 2026 earnings TOMORROW, Aug 11, 2026. The stock has run hard into the print, up 11.0% on Aug 7 alone to $26.71, extending gains that trace back partly to the successful Alpha Flight 7 launch (Mar 2026, +12.77% same-day) which validated key Block II upgrades ahead of the full Block II debut still planned for Flight 8. FY26 guidance ($420-450M, 80% pre-booked via a $1.3B backlog) should still hold from the Q1 print; the real swing factor tomorrow is execution commentary and any update on Alpha Block II's still-undated Flight 8 debut. Consensus (MarketBeat, 12 analysts) sits at $40.64 (~52% upside from here), with a $60 high estimate.

catalysts.description: Follow-up to Blue Ghost 1's successful Mar 2025 Moon landing, still targeted for late 2026. Separately, a $144M NASA CLPS contract (Jun 30) funds an accelerated future Blue Ghost mission targeted for 2028.

risks: Alpha's mishap history is real — Flight 7 (Mar 2026) validated key Block II sub-components, but the FULL Block II configuration hasn't flown yet (still targeted 'late summer', no confirmed date); a Flight 8 failure would hit the stock hard

Extreme realized volatility: FLY has swung across a wide 52-week range, including single-day moves of +12.8% (Mar 11 Flight 7), +17.8% (Jun 11), -19.1% (Jun 12), and now +11.0% (Aug 7) — genuinely high-beta even for a space-launch small-cap
